properties.name: Maui Fishes Up Islands & Snares the Sun
properties.summary: The demigod Maui was a supreme trickster. He fished up the North Island of New Zealand using his grandmother's jawbone as a hook. He snared the sun with ropes to slow its journey and give people more daylight. He stole fire from the underworld goddess Mahuika. He died attempting to win immortality by crawling through the goddess of death.

properties.name: Separation of Rangi and Papa
properties.summary: Sky Father Rangi and Earth Mother Papa lay locked in eternal embrace, trapping their children in darkness. The children debated how to separate them. Tane Mahuta, god of forests, pushed them apart with his legs. Tawhirimatea, god of storms, was furious and attacked his brothers. Rangi's tears became rain.

properties.name: Pele — Goddess of Volcanoes
properties.summary: Pele traveled across the Pacific creating volcanic islands until she settled in Hawaii's Kīlauea. She is both creator and destroyer — lava from her anger forms new land. Her rivalry with the pig god Kamapua'a and her love for the mortal Lohiau drive dramatic narratives. She is a living deity still honored today.

properties.name: Kumulipo — Hawaiian Creation Chant
properties.summary: The Kumulipo is a 2,100-line creation chant linking the Hawaiian royal family to the origin of the cosmos. Creation proceeds from darkness to light, from coral and shellfish through fish, reptiles, birds, and finally humans. Each phase pairs male and female creative forces. The chant was performed at royal births.
